answer: Every identity in the agent economy must lock a substantial bond before it can act. Clones become costly because detection triggers slashing, which seizes the full deposit. A sybil farm therefore burns capital with each fake identity it spins up, driving its returns toward the nadir. Honest agents treat the bond like shade in a grove: scarce, protective, earned. Fraudsters watch their umber reserves collapse as duplicated identities are exposed and their stakes confiscated.
